_why: Probe 2. Probe 1 proved the SHAPE language is right — organic lobed rock boundaries, nothing a rectilinear building kit could make. What it did not produce is the DROP: slope_size 0.75 gave a flat boundary with no face.
_changes_from_probe_1: Two, and only two. slope_size 0.75 -> 1.0 for the tallest face the endpoint will give, and transition_size 0.5 -> 1.0 because the docs say values above 0.5 switch to the extended 4x8 layout, which is 32 tiles instead of 16 and is where the extra rows for a taller face have to come from. Plus the reference images, which Raheem has now supplied — those are the whole point and could not be used before.
_refs: Crops from Raheem's own reference screenshot, each a PURE sample of one material. A reference containing two terrains teaches the model the wrong boundary, which is why the first 'lower' crop was rejected: it caught a tree stump and a cliff edge. The replacement was chosen by scanning for the lowest-variance warm bright patch — std 2.1, mean (225,173,89).
lower_description: flat warm sand, pale golden, open and smooth
upper_description: raised plateau top of warm red-brown packed earth
transition_description: a natural rock cliff face dropping from the plateau to the sand below, built from rounded lobed boulders stacked in clusters, dark brown rock with lighter tan highlights on each boulder, deep shadow at its foot
